chunks: And among what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, that he said:
The Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: Allah was not to place menstruation together with pregnancy.

That means: if a woman sees blood while she is pregnant, she does not leave the salat (prayer), unless she sees it at the head of the child, when labor pains strike her; and if she sees blood then, she leaves the salat (prayer).

So these two reports do not contradict the earlier reports, because the first report said: I asked him about a pregnant woman who sees one gush and two gushes during the days and during the month, and he said to him: that is a flowing discharge; this does not prevent her from salat (prayer). That is sound, because that is not the minimum of menstruation, for we have already explained that the minimum days of menstruation are three days. If she sees only one gush or two gushes, then it is not menstrual blood, and it is not permissible for her to leave salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting).

As for the second report, which is his statement عليه السلام, 'Allah did not place pregnancy together with menstruation,' the way to understand it is that this is not the case with a pregnant woman whose pregnancy has become evident. Menstruation only occurs so long as the pregnancy has not become evident; once it becomes evident, menstruation has ceased. For that reason, we held that whenever it is delayed from her usual time by twenty days, then that is not menstrual blood. That is indicated by what...

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer that is not to be left in this case
key_terms.الصَّوْمِ: sawm (fasting), which is also not to be left when the blood is not menstrual
key_terms.الْهِرَاقَةُ: a flowing discharge or bleeding that is not treated as menstruation here
key_terms.حَبَلٍ: pregnancy; the state of carrying a child
key_terms.حَيْضًا: menstruation; menstrual bleeding with legal consequences for worship
key_terms.دَمِ حَيْضٍ: menstrual blood in the legal sense

ai.seo_question: Does blood seen during pregnancy count as menstruation in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling concerning blood seen by a pregnant woman and its effect on salat (prayer) and sawm (fasting). It explains that slight blood discharge does not count as menstrual blood, and reconciles reports by distinguishing between early, non-evident pregnancy and pregnancy that has become evident.
